edges.description: This node names viral infection in its own text as a trigger acting in genetically susceptible individuals, so the exposure is the node's own content. The evidence is unusually deep for this backfill, and the two items carried here are the two that do different work: one takes the virus as far as the beta cell, and the other is the single infection the literature treats as settled rather than candidate.

Named at the same node as viral infection but graded below it throughout, because the evidence points both ways and the entry already records that. The refuting item is carried on the link deliberately rather than left in the exposure block: the TRIGR trial removed intact cow's milk protein from infant feeding, measured type 1 diabetes itself, and found no reduction over a median of 11.5 years. Keeping it here means the negative result travels with the claim rather than sitting where a reader of the pathograph would never meet it. An earlier version of this link carried a different negative trial summary whose endpoint was celiac disease rather than this disease; that item has no bearing on the claim and was removed.
